The share of closes that are tracker rises with the EV floor: 39% (all window) 45% (1%) 54% (2%) 61% (2.5%) 68% (3%) 70% (4%), so 'CLV climbs monotonically with the floor' is partly a source-mix effect. Rest of window on independent closes n=105: +0.30% (41% of EV kept). Excess hi minus lo on independent closes +1.55pp [0.48, 2.71] (52 games); first half +1.23pp [0.28, 2.15] (19 vs 96 bets, 43 games); second half +2.6pp [-1.8, +7.5] (4 vs 9 bets, 9 games: uninformative). So 'the second half agrees' is the same tracker re-read, not independent. Placed-bet ROI check: rule bets WITH a close ROI -15.2% [-40.0, +9.9] (77 settled, 34 games); WITHOUT a close +33.6% [11.7, 56.5] (77 settled, 29 games): CLV and ROI do not line up (noise: the two halves differ by 49 pts). Family-wise on independent closes only: max excess over 6 EV floors (1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4%) = +1.55pp at 2%; naive bet-level permutation p=0.077; game-level permutation (game-mean EV permuted among 52 games) p=0.033. Builder's tried_count (9340) vs the 5,074 rules in its max-t statement vs 475 in the within-window test are three different families and are not reconciled in the brief.
reason: The numbers reproduce exactly (161 bets, 51 games, CLV +3.01% [2.12, 4.19] on 79 closes/34 games, halves +2.70% and +4.35%) but they overstate the evidence. (1) 54% of the closes (43 of 79) are tracker re-reads of CNO's own consensus fair on bets that were already PLACED (CLV +4.03% vs listed EV +3.97%): that checks that the fair persisted for minutes, it is not a closing line, and its share grows with the EV floor, which builds the 'CLV climbs with the floor' pattern and passes every vs-zero test by construction. (2) On independent closes (ESPN/Pinnacle/Novig 3+ trades) the rule is +1.86% on only 23 bets/16 games (16 of them Novig trades, only 7 ESPN/Pinnacle), excess over the rest of the window +1.55pp [0.48, 2.71], single-test p about 0.02-0.03 and not family-wise convincing (game-level permutation over 6 floors p=0.033, iid p=0.077) after a search over thousands of rules. (3) The second half is one day (Oct 5), 12 games, 15 closes in 8 games, 11 of them tracker, 4 ESPN: it contains no independent confirmation (independent excess +2.6pp, CI [-1.8, +7.5], 4 vs 9 bets). (4) ROI +9.2% [-9.2, +26.7] confirms nothing; the with-close subset lost -15.2%. Verdict: a modest real signal is plausible (first half independent excess +1.2pp, internal CNO fair stable, nothing contradicts it) but it is NOT established; if put to Tj it must be as an open question with the independent-close CLV as the claim (about +1.9%), not +3.0%.
caveats: To settle it on independent closes alone: sd of per-game mean CLV is 2.6 pts; detecting a +1.55pp excess at 80% power needs about 44 games with an independent close per arm, a +1.0pp excess about 105; a +/-1pp CI on the rule's independent CLV needs about 26 games (it has 16). The study yields about 22.6 games/day of this rule but only about 14% of its bets (23 of 161) have an independent close.

Next-morning data would fix part of it: Oct 5 and later games get Novig trades closes the morning after (the second half has none yet); re-run on the next scan-study file before deciding. Logging a Pinnacle/sharp-book read at the start for every listed bet (not only placed ones) would give prop closes.

Tracker-source CLV is measured only on bets Tj or the auto-bet placed (placed rate 31% of the rule's bets in the first half, 21% in the second); their selection depends on the app's own rules at placement time, so it is not a random sample of the rule.

51% of rule bets have no close (82/161); close availability depends on source (props: Pinnacle file rarely has them; ESPN game lines only), so the CLV sample is mostly props that Tj placed or that had 3+ Novig trades.

Near-start bets: independent closes for bets first listed under 30 min before start show +0.19% (n=9, 7 games) vs +1.9 to +3.5% for 30-360 min (n=14): the 6 h window's CLV also depends on horizon (shorter time to drift), not only on EV.

Concentration: NFL is 55% of the rule's bets (46 of 79 closes, 12 games, CLV +2.6%), props 81% (63 of 79 closes, 25 games, +2.8%); NHL +4.5% on 17 closes/11 games; one game holds 16 of the 79 closes (20%) but dropping it raises CLV to +3.4%.
The rule is the same population as the app's CNO list at EV floor of at least 2% (79.5% shown); rule 3 (EV>=2.5%) is nested in it: 122 bets, 64 closes, CLV +3.01%, independent n=13 (10 games) +1.64%.
Any adoption is a question for Tj (it changes which bets are listed or placed); nothing here argues for loosening a safety limit, and the rule is stricter than today's CNO floor of 1%.
